title: Flood Risk Mapping and the Distributional Impacts of Climate Information
abstract: This paper examines the provision of official flood risk information in the United States and its distributional impacts on residential flood insurance take-up. Assembling all flood maps produced after Hurricane Katrina, I document that updated maps decreased the number of properties zoned in high-risk floodplains and incorrectly omitted five million properties, primarily in neighborhoods with more Black and Hispanic residents. Leveraging the staggered timing of map updates, I estimate that updated maps decreased flood insurance take-up and exacerbated racial disparities in insurance coverage. While past map updates distorted risk and price signals, correcting flood maps would yield substantial welfare gains. (JEL D83, G22, G52, J15, Q54)
abstract_zh: 本文考察了美国官方洪水风险信息的提供情况及其对住宅洪水保险参保率的分配影响。在汇集了卡特里娜飓风之后绘制的所有洪水地图后，我发现，地图更新减少了被划入高风险洪泛区的房产数量，并错误地遗漏了500万处房产，这些房产主要位于黑人和西班牙裔居民较多的社区。利用地图更新的交错时间，我估计地图更新降低了洪水保险的参保率，并加剧了保险覆盖中的种族差距。虽然过去的地图更新扭曲了风险和价格信号，但纠正洪水地图将带来可观的福利收益。（JEL D83, G22, G52, J15, Q54）

title: Managing Unpriced Climate Risks in US Housing Markets
venue: Review of Environmental Economics and Policy
abstract: Climate risks are not fully priced in US housing markets. This mispricing can distort household decision-making and may create perverse incentives for development in high-risk areas. Unpriced climate risk could also cause sudden adjustments in home values when consumers’ perceptions of climate risks change, creating market instability. To improve the economic efficiency of housing markets, state and federal policies are needed to correct the market failures underlying this mispricing. However, depending on how they are implemented, certain policy interventions could introduce destabilizing effects and may worsen socioeconomic inequality. To support policy makers navigating these trade-offs, we review how policies that contribute toward more efficient pricing of climate risk can either support or hinder market stability and progressive distributional outcomes. We specifically focus on how three sets of state and federal policy levers—improving climate risk information, removing subsidies for development in high-risk areas, and increasing public investment in disaster risk reduction—can be implemented to reprice climate risk in housing markets following a gradual and transparent pathway, while protecting low-income households from adverse financial impacts.
abstract_zh: 美国住房市场中的气候风险并未得到充分定价。这种错误定价可能扭曲家庭决策，并可能对高风险地区的开发产生错误激励。当消费者对气候风险的认知发生变化时，未定价的气候风险还可能导致房产价值的突然调整，从而造成市场不稳定。为提高住房市场的经济效率，需要州和联邦政策来纠正导致这种错误定价的市场失灵。然而，根据具体实施方式的不同，某些政策干预可能产生破坏性影响，并可能加剧社会经济不平等。为帮助政策制定者应对这些权衡，我们回顾了有助于更有效地为气候风险定价的政策，如何既可能支持，也可能阻碍市场稳定和累进性的分配结果。我们特别关注三类州和联邦政策工具（改善气候风险信息、取消对高风险地区开发的补贴，以及增加灾害风险降低的公共投资），探讨如何以渐进、透明的路径实施这些工具，从而重新为住房市场中的气候风险定价，同时保护低收入家庭免受不利的财务影响。

Unpriced Climate Risk and the Potential Consequences of Overvaluation in US Housing Markets
abstract: Climate change impacts threaten the stability of the US housing market. In response to growing concerns that increasing costs of flooding are not fully captured in property values, we quantify the magnitude of unpriced flood risk in the housing market by comparing the empirical and economically efficient prices for properties at risk. We find that residential properties exposed to flood risk are overvalued by US$121–US$237 billion, depending on the discount rate. In general, highly overvalued properties are concentrated in counties along the coast with no flood risk disclosure laws and where there is less concern about climate change. Low-income households are at greater risk of losing home equity from price deflation, and municipalities that are heavily reliant on property taxes for revenue are vulnerable to budgetary shortfalls. The consequences of these financial risks will depend on policy choices that influence who bears the costs of climate change.
abstract_zh: 气候变化影响威胁着美国房地产市场的稳定。鉴于人们日益担忧洪水成本的上升未被房产价值充分反映，我们通过比较风险房产的实际价格与经济效率价格，量化了房地产市场中未定价洪水风险的规模。我们发现，面临洪水风险的住宅房产被高估了1,210亿至2,370亿美元，具体取决于贴现率。总体而言，被严重高估的房产集中在沿海县，这些县没有洪水风险披露法规，且对气候变化的关注度较低。低收入家庭面临因房价下跌而丧失房屋净值的更大风险，而严重依赖房产税收入的市镇则面临预算短缺的脆弱性。这些金融风险的后果将取决于那些决定气候变化成本由谁承担的政策选择。

title: Amphibian Collapses Increased Malaria Incidence in Central America
Exposures and Behavioural Responses to Wildfire Smoke
abstract: Pollution from wildfires constitutes a growing source of poor air quality globally. To protect health, governments largely rely on citizens to limit their own wildfire smoke exposures, but the effectiveness of this strategy is hard to observe. Using data from private pollution sensors, cell phones, social media posts and internet search activity, we find that during large wildfire smoke events, individuals in wealthy locations increasingly search for information about air quality and health protection, stay at home more and are unhappier. Residents of lower-income neighbourhoods exhibit similar patterns in searches for air quality information but not for health protection, spend less time at home and have more muted sentiment responses. During smoke events, indoor particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations often remain 3–4× above health-based guidelines and vary by 20× between neighbouring households. Our results suggest that policy reliance on self-protection to mitigate smoke health risks will have modest and unequal benefits. Burke et al. show that smoke exposure is associated with behavioural changes and worsening sentiment, with important differences by income. They document substantial infiltration of smoke into homes, suggesting that current policy reliance on self-protection could be ineffective.
abstract_zh: 野火产生的污染日益成为全球空气质量恶化的一大来源。为保护健康，各国政府在很大程度上依赖公民自行限制其野火烟雾暴露，但这一策略的有效性难以观察。利用私人污染传感器、手机、社交媒体帖子和网络搜索活动数据，我们发现，在大规模野火烟雾事件期间，富裕地区的个人越来越多地搜索空气质量和健康防护信息，更多地待在家中，且更加不快乐。低收入社区的居民在空气质量信息搜索方面表现出类似模式，但在健康防护搜索方面并非如此，他们在家中的时间减少，情绪反应也较为平淡。在烟雾事件期间，室内细颗粒物（PM2.5）浓度往往仍比基于健康的指南值高出3至4倍，且相邻家庭之间的差异可达20倍。我们的研究结果表明，依赖自我防护来减轻烟雾健康风险的政策，其效果将是有限的，且收益分配不均。Burke等人表明，烟雾暴露与行为改变及情绪恶化相关，且因收入不同而存在重要差异。他们记录了烟雾大量渗入住宅的情况，表明当前依赖自我防护的政策可能无效。
